title: In-memory Database Cargo Culting
pattern: Moving an analytical or data-intensive workload to an in-memory database under the assumption that RAM access inherently eliminates query performance bottlenecks.
why_bad: The performance advantage of in-memory databases is not due to avoiding disk reads (as disk-based databases cache active blocks anyway), but avoiding the overhead of serialization. If queries trigger massive full table scans, performance remains poor.
detection: Migrating to in-memory storage engines for complex, unindexed search queries or multi-million record aggregates.
counterexample: In-memory key-value caches using direct key lookup indexes.
fix: Ensure transactional indexes are configured, or use a column-oriented storage engine designed for bulk scans.
